note: Reviewed fingerprints of the registered assurance claims. A change here means a statement, its assumptions, or a definition it depends on changed and was reviewed; it does not by itself say the new statement is adequate.

Fir.SimulationS.refines.summary: A simulation with stuttering gives refinement of Decided functions.
Fir.SimulationS.refines.statement:
∀ {R : Nat → Fir.Machine → Fir.Machine → Prop},
  Fir.SimulationS R →
    (∀ (n : Nat) (mt ms : Fir.Machine),
        R n mt ms → Fir.Events.Refines mt.core.trace ms.core.trace) →
      ∀ {mod : Fir.Module} {tgt src : Fir.Func},
        (∀ (oracle : Fir.Oracle) (world : Fir.World) (args : List Fir.RVal),
            ∃ oracle',
              Fir.InitMatch (fun mt ms => ∃ n, R n mt ms)
                (Fir.Machine.init oracle world mod tgt args)
                (Fir.Machine.init oracle' world mod src args)) →
          Fir.Func.Decided mod src → Fir.Func.Refines mod tgt src
Fir.SimulationS.refines.name: Fir.SimulationS.refines

Fir.Simulation.refines.summary: A lockstep simulation from every related start gives refinement of Decided functions.
Fir.Simulation.refines.statement:
∀ {R : Fir.Machine → Fir.Machine → Prop},
  Fir.Simulation R →
    (∀ (mt ms : Fir.Machine), R mt ms → Fir.Events.Refines mt.core.trace ms.core.trace) →
      ∀ {mod : Fir.Module} {tgt src : Fir.Func},
        (∀ (oracle : Fir.Oracle) (world : Fir.World) (args : List Fir.RVal),
            ∃ oracle',
              Fir.InitMatch R (Fir.Machine.init oracle world mod tgt args)
                (Fir.Machine.init oracle' world mod src args)) →
          Fir.Func.Decided mod src → Fir.Func.Refines mod tgt src
Fir.Simulation.refines.name: Fir.Simulation.refines

Fir.Rules.mul_two.summary: int.mul.wrap x, 2 is refined by int.add.wrap x, x, for every width and poison.
Fir.Rules.mul_two.statement:
∀ {w : Nat} (x : Fir.Val w),
  (Fir.Sem.arith Fir.ArithOp.add Fir.Ovf.wrap x x).Refines
    (Fir.Sem.arith Fir.ArithOp.mul Fir.Ovf.wrap x (Fir.Sem.const w 2))
Fir.Rules.mul_two.name: Fir.Rules.mul_two

Fir.Rules.add_zero.summary: int.add with 0 is refined by its operand, for every overflow modifier.
Fir.Rules.add_zero.statement:
∀ {w : Nat} (ovf : Fir.Ovf) (x : Fir.Val w),
  (Fir.OpOut.ok x).Refines (Fir.Sem.arith Fir.ArithOp.add ovf x (Fir.Sem.const w 0))
Fir.Rules.add_zero.name: Fir.Rules.add_zero

Fir.Rules.add_nsw_one_sgt.summary: int.cmp.sgt (int.add.nsw x, 1), x is refined by true at widths of at least 2.
Fir.Rules.add_nsw_one_sgt.statement:
∀ {w : Nat},
  2 ≤ w →
    ∀ (x : Fir.Val w),
      (Fir.OpOut.ok (Fir.Sem.const 1 1)).Refines
        ((Fir.Sem.arith Fir.ArithOp.add Fir.Ovf.nsw x (Fir.Sem.const w 1)).bind fun y =>
          Fir.OpOut.ok (Fir.Sem.cmp Fir.Pred.sgt y x))
Fir.Rules.add_nsw_one_sgt.name: Fir.Rules.add_nsw_one_sgt

Fir.Lower.Proof.lowerFunc_refines.summary: The whole lowering of a function refines it where scalarizing and lowering cf.try change nothing. Scalarization, cf.try lowering, and module composition are not proved.
Fir.Lower.Proof.lowerFunc_refines.statement:
∀ {mod : Fir.Module} {ext : List String} {f g : Fir.Func},
  Fir.Lower.lowerFunc mod.space ext f = Except.ok g →
    Fir.Lower.scalarize mod.space f = Except.ok f →
      Fir.Lower.lowerExn ext f = Except.ok f →
        Fir.Lower.Proof.opsVarArgs f.body.ops = true →
          Fir.Lower.Proof.NoTemps f.body.ops → Fir.Func.Decided mod f → Fir.Func.Refines mod g f
Fir.Lower.Proof.lowerFunc_refines.name: Fir.Lower.Proof.lowerFunc_refines

Fir.Lower.Proof.Expand.refines.summary: The HFIR lowering's expansion pass (checked arithmetic, ptr.field, ptr.index) refines each function, given variable operands, no pass temporaries, and a Decided source.
Fir.Lower.Proof.Expand.refines.statement:
∀ {mod : Fir.Module} {f g : Fir.Func},
  Fir.Lower.expand mod.space f = Except.ok g →
    Fir.Lower.Proof.opsVarArgs f.body.ops = true →
      Fir.Lower.Proof.NoTemps f.body.ops → Fir.Func.Decided mod f → Fir.Func.Refines mod g f
Fir.Lower.Proof.Expand.refines.name: Fir.Lower.Proof.Expand.refines

Fir.Fwd.refines.summary: Store-to-load forwarding: a load right after a store of its type through the same pointer variable may read the stored value instead, if the source is Decided.
Fir.Fwd.refines.statement:
∀ {mod : Fir.Module} {tgt src : Fir.Func},
  8 ≤ mod.space.ptrBits →
    tgt.params = src.params →
      tgt.rets = src.rets →
        tgt.variadic = src.variadic →
          Fir.OpsRel Fir.Fwd.L tgt.body.ops src.body.ops →
            Fir.Func.Decided mod src → Fir.Func.Refines mod tgt src
Fir.Fwd.refines.name: Fir.Fwd.refines

Fir.Float.truncInt_ofInt.summary: Integers of at most m + 1 bits convert to a float and back (toward zero) unchanged, when the format's range holds them.
Fir.Float.truncInt_ofInt.statement:
∀ {F : Fir.FloatFmt} {v : Int},
  v.natAbs < 2 ^ (F.m + 1) →
    2 ≤ F.e → F.m + 1 ≤ 2 ^ (F.e - 1) → Fir.Float.truncInt (Fir.Float.ofInt F v) = some v
Fir.Float.truncInt_ofInt.name: Fir.Float.truncInt_ofInt

Fir.Float.round_decode.summary: Rounding a representable value gives its bits back.
Fir.Float.round_decode.statement:
∀ {F : Fir.FloatFmt} {x : Fir.Float.Bits F} {neg : Bool} {n : Nat},
  Fir.Float.decode x = Fir.Float.Num.fin neg n → 2 ≤ F.e → Fir.Float.round F neg n 1 = x
Fir.Float.round_decode.name: Fir.Float.round_decode

Fir.Float.neg_neg.summary: float.neg is an involution on bits.
Fir.Float.neg_neg.statement: ∀ {F : Fir.FloatFmt} (x : Fir.Float.Bits F), Fir.Float.neg (Fir.Float.neg x) = x
Fir.Float.neg_neg.name: Fir.Float.neg_neg

Fir.Float.mul_comm.summary: Float multiplication commutes, up to the NaN payload the oracle picks.
Fir.Float.mul_comm.statement:
∀ {F : Fir.FloatFmt} (o : Int) (x y : Fir.Float.Bits F),
  ∃ o', Fir.Float.mul o x y = Fir.Float.mul o' y x
Fir.Float.mul_comm.name: Fir.Float.mul_comm

Fir.Float.ext_trunc.summary: float.ext then float.trunc is the identity on f32, NaNs aside.
Fir.Float.ext_trunc.statement:
∀ {x : Fir.Float.Bits Fir.FloatTy.f32.fmt},
  Fir.Float.decode x ≠ Fir.Float.Num.nan →
    ∀ (o o' : Int), Fir.Float.cvt Fir.FloatTy.f32.fmt o' (Fir.Float.cvt Fir.FloatTy.f64.fmt o x) = x
Fir.Float.ext_trunc.name: Fir.Float.ext_trunc

Fir.Float.decode_round.summary: A representable number of units rounds to bits that decode to it.
Fir.Float.decode_round.statement:
∀ {F : Fir.FloatFmt} {N c : Nat} {neg : Bool},
  0 < c →
    Fir.Float.Repr F N →
      2 ≤ F.e → Fir.Float.decode (Fir.Float.round F neg (N * c) c) = Fir.Float.Num.fin neg N
Fir.Float.decode_round.name: Fir.Float.decode_round

Fir.Float.cvt_cvt.summary: Widening, then narrowing back, gives every non-NaN value back, whatever NaN choices the oracle makes.
Fir.Float.cvt_cvt.statement:
∀ {F G : Fir.FloatFmt} {x : Fir.Float.Bits F},
  Fir.Float.decode x ≠ Fir.Float.Num.nan →
    ∀ (o o' : Int),
      F.m ≤ G.m →
        F.qneg < G.qneg →
          F.top + (G.qneg - F.qneg) ≤ G.top →
            2 ≤ F.e → 2 ≤ G.e → Fir.Float.cvt F o' (Fir.Float.cvt G o x) = x
Fir.Float.cvt_cvt.name: Fir.Float.cvt_cvt

Fir.Float.add_comm.summary: Float addition commutes, up to the NaN payload the oracle picks.
Fir.Float.add_comm.statement:
∀ {F : Fir.FloatFmt} (o : Int) (x y : Fir.Float.Bits F),
  ∃ o', Fir.Float.add o x y = Fir.Float.add o' y x
Fir.Float.add_comm.name: Fir.Float.add_comm

Fir.Dse.refines.summary: DSE: deleting a store that the next op overwrites through the same pointer variable with a same-size scalar store refines the function, if the source is Decided.
Fir.Dse.refines.statement:
∀ {mod : Fir.Module} {tgt src : Fir.Func},
  tgt.params = src.params →
    tgt.rets = src.rets →
      tgt.variadic = src.variadic →
        Fir.OpsRel Fir.Dse.L tgt.body.ops src.body.ops →
          Fir.Func.Decided mod src → Fir.Func.Refines mod tgt src
Fir.Dse.refines.name: Fir.Dse.refines

Fir.Dce.refines.summary: DCE: deleting pure ops whose results no later op of their region reads, anywhere in a function, gives a function that refines it in the module, if the source is Decided.
Fir.Dce.refines.statement:
∀ {mod : Fir.Module} {tgt src : Fir.Func},
  tgt.params = src.params →
    tgt.rets = src.rets →
      tgt.variadic = src.variadic →
        Fir.OpsRel Fir.Dce.L tgt.body.ops src.body.ops →
          Fir.Func.Decided mod src → Fir.Func.Refines mod tgt src
Fir.Dce.refines.name: Fir.Dce.refines

Fir.Dce.freeze_changes_core.summary: freeze of poison changes the core (it consults the oracle), although its declaration lists no effects: an effects declaration is not evidence of purity.
Fir.Dce.freeze_changes_core.statement:
∀ (loc : Option Fir.Loc) (r : Fir.Result) (w : Nat) (c : Fir.Core),
  ¬Fir.Dce.ReadOnly (Fir.evalSimple loc Fir.OpKind.freeze [r] [Fir.RVal.int w Fir.Val.poison])
Fir.Dce.freeze_changes_core.name: Fir.Dce.freeze_changes_core

Fir.Dce.float_pure.summary: The float ops that can't trap (all but float.to_int.*.trap) are pure: a NaN result is the oracle's choice from the op and its operands, so computing one only reads the core.
Fir.Dce.float_pure.statement:
∀ {k : Fir.OpKind},
  Fir.Dce.floatPure k = true →
    ∀ (res : List Fir.Result) (args : List Fir.Operand),
      (∀ (a : Fir.Operand), a ∈ args → ∃ n, a = Fir.Operand.var n) →
        ∀ (loc : Option Fir.Loc), Fir.Dce.Pure (Fir.Op.mk k res args [] loc)
Fir.Dce.float_pure.name: Fir.Dce.float_pure

Fir.Dce.evalFloat_oracle.summary: Every float op, traps included, depends on the core only through the oracle and leaves the core as it was, so within a run it is a function of its operands.
Fir.Dce.evalFloat_oracle.statement:
∀ (loc : Option Fir.Loc) (k : Fir.OpKind) (rs : List Fir.Result) (vs : List Fir.RVal),
  Fir.Dce.OracleOnly (Fir.evalFloat loc k rs vs)
Fir.Dce.evalFloat_oracle.name: Fir.Dce.evalFloat_oracle

Fir.Dce.dcePerm_sound.summary: Every op kind the generated DCE contract lets the Rust pass delete is pure (PureKind): no call, no stack allocation, not a terminator, and its computation only reads the core and fails only by UB or getting stuck.
Fir.Dce.dcePerm_sound.statement: ∀ (k : Fir.OpKind), Fir.Dce.dcePerm k = Fir.Dce.DcePerm.delete → Fir.Dce.PureKind k
Fir.Dce.dcePerm_sound.name: Fir.Dce.dcePerm_sound

Fir.Dce.checkFunc_sound.summary: If the DCE checker run by fir-ref check-dce accepts a target function for a Decided source function, the target refines the source in the source module.
Fir.Dce.checkFunc_sound.statement:
∀ {mod : Fir.Module} {tgt src : Fir.Func},
  Fir.Dce.checkFunc tgt src = true → Fir.Func.Decided mod src → Fir.Func.Refines mod tgt src
Fir.Dce.checkFunc_sound.name: Fir.Dce.checkFunc_sound

Fir.CopyProp.refines.summary: Copy propagation through straight-line code (up to the first op with regions or a call) refines the function, if the source is Decided.
Fir.CopyProp.refines.statement:
∀ {mod : Fir.Module} {tgt src : Fir.Func},
  tgt.params = src.params →
    tgt.rets = src.rets →
      tgt.variadic = src.variadic →
        Fir.OpsRel Fir.CopyProp.L tgt.body.ops src.body.ops →
          Fir.Func.Decided mod src → Fir.Func.Refines mod tgt src
Fir.CopyProp.refines.name: Fir.CopyProp.refines

Fir.AArch64.roundTrip.summary: A struct or array passed in registers (an HFA or up to 16 bytes) arrives with its defined bytes exactly: its pieces, each loaded into a register and stored back, are its bytes; a word of eight fragments of one pointer stays that pointer. That native code passes exactly these pieces where Fir.AArch64.argLocs says is tested (the ABI torture test), not proved.
Fir.AArch64.roundTrip.statement:
∀ {sp : Fir.SpaceCfg} {t : Fir.Ty} {bs : List Fir.Byte},
  bs.length = Fir.Ty.size sp t →
    ((∃ n e, Fir.AArch64.passKind sp t = Fir.AArch64.PassKind.words n e) ∨
        ∃ f n, Fir.AArch64.passKind sp t = Fir.AArch64.PassKind.hfa f n) →
      (∀ (pc : List Fir.Byte),
          pc ∈ Fir.AArch64.pieces (Fir.AArch64.passKind sp t) bs →
            (Fir.AArch64.Word.ofBytes? pc).isSome = true) →
        (List.map
              (fun pc =>
                (Option.map (fun x => Fir.AArch64.Word.bytes pc.length x)
                      (Fir.AArch64.Word.ofBytes? pc)).getD
                  [])
              (Fir.AArch64.pieces (Fir.AArch64.passKind sp t) bs)).flatten =
          bs
Fir.AArch64.roundTrip.name: Fir.AArch64.roundTrip

Fir.AArch64.ptrLeaf_inReg.summary: In a composite passed as x-register words that doesn't split a pointer (Ty.splitsPtr, which instruction selection refuses), a pointer leaf's register holds that pointer, provenance included, whatever the other pieces hold.
Fir.AArch64.ptrLeaf_inReg.statement:
∀ {sp : Fir.SpaceCfg} {t : Fir.Ty} {bs : List Fir.Byte} {n : Nat} {e : Bool},
  Fir.AArch64.passKind sp t = Fir.AArch64.PassKind.words n e →
    Fir.Ty.splitsPtr sp t = false →
      bs.length = Fir.Ty.size sp t →
        ∀ {o : Nat},
          (o, Fir.Ty.ptr) ∈ Fir.Ty.leaves sp t →
            ∀ {p : Fir.Ptr},
              List.take 8 (List.drop o bs) = List.map (Fir.Byte.frag p) (List.range 8) →
                ∀ {ws : List Fir.AArch64.Word},
                  Fir.AArch64.Word.HoldAll (Fir.AArch64.pieces (Fir.AArch64.passKind sp t) bs) ws →
                    ws[o / 8]? = some (Fir.AArch64.Word.ptr p)
Fir.AArch64.ptrLeaf_inReg.name: Fir.AArch64.ptrLeaf_inReg

Fir.AArch64.pieces_flatten.summary: The register pieces of a composite passed in registers (8-byte words, or an HFA's members), joined, are its bytes.
Fir.AArch64.pieces_flatten.statement:
∀ {sp : Fir.SpaceCfg} {t : Fir.Ty} {bs : List Fir.Byte},
  bs.length = Fir.Ty.size sp t →
    ((∃ n e, Fir.AArch64.passKind sp t = Fir.AArch64.PassKind.words n e) ∨
        ∃ f n, Fir.AArch64.passKind sp t = Fir.AArch64.PassKind.hfa f n) →
      (Fir.AArch64.pieces (Fir.AArch64.passKind sp t) bs).flatten = bs
Fir.AArch64.pieces_flatten.name: Fir.AArch64.pieces_flatten

Fir.AArch64.fpSqrt_allowed.summary: fsqrt gives a result float.sqrt allows.
Fir.AArch64.fpSqrt_allowed.statement: ∀ {F : Fir.FloatFmt} (x : Fir.Float.Bits F), ∃ o, Fir.AArch64.fpSqrt x = Fir.Float.sqrt o x
Fir.AArch64.fpSqrt_allowed.name: Fir.AArch64.fpSqrt_allowed

Fir.AArch64.fpMulAdd_allowed.summary: fmadd gives a result float.fma allows, its addend last.
Fir.AArch64.fpMulAdd_allowed.statement:
∀ {F : Fir.FloatFmt} (a n m : Fir.Float.Bits F),
  ∃ o, Fir.AArch64.fpMulAdd a n m = Fir.Float.fma o n m a
Fir.AArch64.fpMulAdd_allowed.name: Fir.AArch64.fpMulAdd_allowed

Fir.AArch64.fpConvert_allowed.summary: fcvt gives a result float.ext and float.trunc allow.
Fir.AArch64.fpConvert_allowed.statement: ∀ {F G : Fir.FloatFmt} (x : Fir.Float.Bits F), ∃ o, Fir.AArch64.fpConvert G x = Fir.Float.cvt G o x
Fir.AArch64.fpConvert_allowed.name: Fir.AArch64.fpConvert_allowed

Fir.AArch64.fpAlu_allowed.summary: fadd, fsub, fmul, and fdiv give results float.add and friends allow (for some oracle answer).
Fir.AArch64.fpAlu_allowed.statement:
∀ {F : Fir.FloatFmt} (op : Fir.FAluOp) (x y : Fir.Float.Bits F),
  ∃ o, Fir.AArch64.fpAlu op x y = op.float o x y
Fir.AArch64.fpAlu_allowed.name: Fir.AArch64.fpAlu_allowed

Fir.AArch64.floatSqrt_arm.summary: Under Arm's NaN choice, float.sqrt is fsqrt.
Fir.AArch64.floatSqrt_arm.statement:
∀ {f : Fir.FloatTy} (a : BitVec f.width),
  Fir.Sem.floatUn f.fmt Fir.FUnOp.sqrt
      (Fir.AArch64.armNan (Fir.OpKind.floatUn Fir.FUnOp.sqrt) [Fir.RVal.float f (Fir.Val.bits a)])
      (Fir.Val.bits a) =
    Fir.Val.bits (Fir.AArch64.fpSqrt a)
Fir.AArch64.floatSqrt_arm.name: Fir.AArch64.floatSqrt_arm

Fir.AArch64.floatFma_arm.summary: Under Arm's NaN choice, float.fma a, b, c is fmadd with addend c.
Fir.AArch64.floatFma_arm.statement:
∀ {f : Fir.FloatTy} (a b c : BitVec f.width),
  Fir.Sem.floatFma f.fmt
      (Fir.AArch64.armNan Fir.OpKind.floatFma
        [Fir.RVal.float f (Fir.Val.bits a), Fir.RVal.float f (Fir.Val.bits b),
          Fir.RVal.float f (Fir.Val.bits c)])
      (Fir.Val.bits a) (Fir.Val.bits b) (Fir.Val.bits c) =
    Fir.Val.bits (Fir.AArch64.fpMulAdd c a b)
Fir.AArch64.floatFma_arm.name: Fir.AArch64.floatFma_arm

Fir.AArch64.floatExt_arm.summary: Under Arm's NaN choice, float.ext and float.trunc are fcvt.
Fir.AArch64.floatExt_arm.statement:
∀ (a : BitVec Fir.FloatTy.f32.width),
  Fir.Sem.floatCvt Fir.FloatTy.f32.fmt Fir.FloatTy.f64.fmt
      (Fir.AArch64.armNan Fir.OpKind.floatExt [Fir.RVal.float Fir.FloatTy.f32 (Fir.Val.bits a)])
      (Fir.Val.bits a) =
    Fir.Val.bits (Fir.AArch64.fpConvert Fir.FloatTy.f64.fmt a)
Fir.AArch64.floatExt_arm.name: Fir.AArch64.floatExt_arm

Fir.AArch64.floatBin_arm.summary: Under Arm's NaN choice, float.add and friends are fadd and friends.
Fir.AArch64.floatBin_arm.statement:
∀ {f : Fir.FloatTy} {op : Fir.FBinOp} {o : Fir.FAluOp},
  op.arm = some o →
    ∀ (a b : BitVec f.width),
      Fir.Sem.floatBin f.fmt op
          (Fir.AArch64.armNan (Fir.OpKind.floatBin op)
            [Fir.RVal.float f (Fir.Val.bits a), Fir.RVal.float f (Fir.Val.bits b)])
          (Fir.Val.bits a) (Fir.Val.bits b) =
        Fir.Val.bits (Fir.AArch64.fpAlu o a b)
Fir.AArch64.floatBin_arm.name: Fir.AArch64.floatBin_arm

Fir.AArch64.fcvtz_sat.summary: fcvtzs and fcvtzu are float.to_int.s.sat and float.to_int.u.sat.
Fir.AArch64.fcvtz_sat.statement:
∀ {F : Fir.FloatFmt} (signed : Bool) (n : Nat) (x : Fir.Float.Bits F),
  Fir.Sem.floatToInt F signed Fir.CvtEdge.sat n (Fir.Val.bits x) =
    Fir.OpOut.ok (Fir.Val.bits (Fir.AArch64.fpToInt signed n x))
Fir.AArch64.fcvtz_sat.name: Fir.AArch64.fcvtz_sat

Fir.AArch64.arrives.summary: A struct or array passed in registers arrives with every defined byte in place even when its pieces are partly undefined (padding or poison leaves): any words that hold its pieces (Word.Holds), stored back, give as many bytes with each defined one unchanged.
Fir.AArch64.arrives.statement:
∀ {sp : Fir.SpaceCfg} {t : Fir.Ty} {bs : List Fir.Byte},
  bs.length = Fir.Ty.size sp t →
    ((∃ n e, Fir.AArch64.passKind sp t = Fir.AArch64.PassKind.words n e) ∨
        ∃ f n, Fir.AArch64.passKind sp t = Fir.AArch64.PassKind.hfa f n) →
      ∀ {ws : List Fir.AArch64.Word},
        Fir.AArch64.Word.HoldAll (Fir.AArch64.pieces (Fir.AArch64.passKind sp t) bs) ws →
          Fir.AArch64.Agrees
            (List.zipWith (fun pc w => Fir.AArch64.Word.bytes pc.length w)
                (Fir.AArch64.pieces (Fir.AArch64.passKind sp t) bs) ws).flatten
            bs
Fir.AArch64.arrives.name: Fir.AArch64.arrives

Fir.AArch64.Word.holds_fill.summary: The machine's word for a piece (Word.fill, the shape of AArch64Machine's wordOfBytes: an arbitrary choice for poison and stray fragment bytes) holds it: a whole pointer's eight fragments are that pointer, and every defined byte is in the register. That wordOfBytes is this function is by inspection, not proved.
Fir.AArch64.Word.holds_fill.statement:
∀ (c : Nat → Nat) {pc : List Fir.Byte},
  pc.length ≤ 8 → Fir.AArch64.Word.Holds pc (Fir.AArch64.Word.fill c pc)
Fir.AArch64.Word.holds_fill.name: Fir.AArch64.Word.holds_fill
